Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api

Class Interop

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api.Interop
public final class Interop extends Object
The bridge between Java (and Kotlin) values and Mandela values.

A scripting language is only useful inside a JVM host if crossing the boundary is a method call rather than a ritual. This class makes the crossing two calls — toMandela(java.lang.Object) on the way in, toJava(java.lang.Object) on the way out — and both are total: they either produce a value a script can use or throw a MandelaError that names the type that did not fit, because the failure a host sees at the boundary is the only one it will ever see.

The mapping

Java / Kotlin to Mandela
Java / KotlinMandela
nullNull
BooleanBool
Byte/Short/Integer/LongInt (a long)
Float/Double/BigDecimalDouble
String / Character / CharSequenceStr
any CollectionList, elements converted
an arrayList, elements converted
a Map with string-ish keysMap, values converted
a Callable (script function, host function)unchanged
anything with one public invoke method — a Kotlin lambda, a Groovy closure — or one abstract method — a java.util.function type, any single-abstract-method object a HostFunction that calls it
anything elserefused, with the class name in the message

Refusing the last row is the load-bearing decision. A host could wrap an arbitrary object and let a script poke at its fields, and some languages do; that is how a script ends up reading System.out.getClass() .getProtectionDomain() and how a sandbox is quietly bypassed. Here a Java object reaches a script only through a HostFunction the host wrote, or through a conversion the host asked for by name — and both are visible in the host's own source, which is what a reviewer and Capabilities.allowsJvm(java.lang.String) can reason about.

Kotlin

Kotlin needs no special case. A Kotlin fun reference or lambda compiles to a kotlin.jvm.functions.FunctionN whose single abstract method is invoke, so the reflective row above covers it, and Kotlin's List/Map are java.util types by the time they reach the JVM. A Kotlin host writes:


 val engine = Mandela.engine().bind("greet") { name: String -> "hi $name" }.build()
 engine.run("greet(\"world\")")

…because Function1 arrives as something with an invoke, and toMandela turns the returned String into a Str on the way back. Java hosts get the same courtesy through java.util.function: a Function, Predicate, Consumer, Supplier or UnaryOperator is a single-abstract-method object, so bind("upper", String::toUpperCase) works as written, and fn(java.lang.String, java.util.function.Function<java.lang.Object[], java.lang.Object>), fn1(java.lang.String, java.util.function.Function<java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object>) and friends remain the way to name a function the script should see.

  • Method Details

    • toMandela

      public static Object toMandela(Object value)
      Converts a Java or Kotlin value into the Mandela value a script reads.

      The rule lives in HostValues, because the runtime applies exactly the same one when a host calls bind or call: two rules that could disagree would make the same List a list in one snippet and an error in the next. This is the name a host writes, and the one the embedding documentation quotes.

      Parameters:
      value - the host value; may be null
      Returns:
      the same value when it already is one, or its Mandela form
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when there is no honest Mandela form for it

    • toMandelaAll

      public static List<Object> toMandelaAll(Object... values)
      Converts several values at once, the shape a host function's argument list arrives in.
      Parameters:
      values - the host values
      Returns:
      the Mandela values, in order

    • toJava

      public static Object toJava(Object value)
      Converts a Mandela value back into the plain Java form.

      Lists become ArrayLists and maps become LinkedHashMaps, so a host can hold onto the result after the script is finished with it; everything else is already a Java object. Use toJava(Object, Class) when the host wants a specific type.

      Parameters:
      value - the value a script produced
      Returns:
      the Java form

    • toJava

      public static <T> T toJava(Object value, Class<T> type)
      Converts a Mandela value and asks for a particular Java type.

      Four targets cover what a host normally wants; anything else is a cast, and a wrong cast says so instead of quietly returning a String.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the requested type
      Parameters:
      value - the script's value
      type - String.class, Long.class/Integer.class, Double.class, Boolean.class, a List or a Map
      Returns:
      the converted value, or null when value is null
      Throws:
      MandelaError - when the value has no form of the requested type

    • fn

      public static Callable fn(String name, Function<Object[],Object> body)
      Wraps a Java or Kotlin lambda as a script callable.

      The arguments arrive already converted, and whatever the lambda returns is converted on the way out, so a host writes bind("upper", (Function<String, String> String::toUpperCase)) and the script sees a function from Str to Str.

      Parameters:
      name - the name the script calls it by, used in diagnostics
      body - the implementation, in Java values
      Returns:
      a callable to bind on a Runtime
